userStories.title: Project scaffold with health endpoint and Docker image
userStories.description: A TypeScript project with Hono, SQLite, a test runner and a Dockerfile. The running container answers a health endpoint. This proves the toolchain, the test setup and the packaging end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: A test hitting the health endpoint in-process passes
npm test runs the test suite
The Docker image builds and the container serves the health endpoint
The SQLite file location is configurable and intended for a mounted volume

userStories.title: Create a draw and receive personal links
userStories.description: A creator fills in a title, their own name, 2 to 10 options and the other participants' names, and receives one personal link per participant including their own. Covers domain validation, persistence, the create endpoint and the Dutch create page.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating a draw with valid input returns a draw id and one link per participant, each with a distinct unguessable key
Fewer than 2 or more than 10 options is rejected
Duplicate options (ignoring case and surrounding whitespace) and empty options are rejected
Option labels over 100 characters are rejected
Duplicate or empty participant names are rejected
The creator is stored as accepted at creation, all others as not accepted
The create page shows the links with copy buttons and stores the creator's link in a cookie
All user-facing text comes from one Dutch strings file

userStories.title: Open a participant link and see the pending draw
userStories.description: A participant opens their personal link on any device and sees the title, all options with their odds, all participant names and who has accepted. Wrong or unknown links show the same neutral not-found page.
acceptanceCriteria: A valid link returns the draw as seen by that participant, including their own identity
Odds are shown per option as 1 in N
The response never contains any participant's key
An unknown draw id and a wrong key give an identical not-found response
The page shows who has accepted and when the pending draw expires
The same link works from a different device with no cookie

userStories.title: Accept and trigger the draw when everyone has accepted
userStories.description: A participant accepts with one tap. When the last participant accepts, the server picks one option uniformly with a CSPRNG and stores the result permanently. The drawn state never changes afterwards.
acceptanceCriteria: Accepting marks only the acting participant as accepted
Accepting twice is harmless and returns the current state
The draw happens exactly when the last participant accepts, not before
The picked option comes from the injected picker in tests and from crypto.randomInt in production
A statistical test shows every option is reachable and picks are always valid indexes
A drawn draw shows the result, title, options, names and drawn time
No transition can leave the drawn state
Two racing requests are resolved with the first one winning inside a transaction

userStories.title: Reveal animation on each participant's first view
userStories.description: The first time a participant loads the drawn result, they get an animated reveal and the server records revealed_at for them. Later views show the result statically. Works even if the participant opens the link days after the draw.
acceptanceCriteria: The first fetch of a drawn result for a participant returns reveal true and records revealed_at
Every later fetch for that participant returns reveal false
Reveal state is tracked independently per participant
The page plays the animation only when reveal is true and lands on the stored result
Opening the link on a second device after the first reveal shows the result statically

userStories.title: Decline and cancel
userStories.description: A participant can decline, which ends the draw for everyone. The creator can cancel while the draw is pending. Both end states are shown clearly to every participant.
acceptanceCriteria: Declining a pending draw moves it to declined for everyone
Only the creator can cancel, and only while pending
Accepting after decline, cancel or expiry is rejected with the current state
Declining or cancelling after the draw is rejected and the result is unchanged
Each participant's page explains whether the draw was declined or cancelled
A race between cancel and the last accept is resolved with the first request winning

userStories.title: Expiry and retention sweeper
userStories.description: Pending draws expire after 7 days. Drawn results and declined or cancelled draws are deleted 30 days after they ended. A periodic sweeper applies both rules using an injectable clock.
acceptanceCriteria: A pending draw older than 7 days becomes expired and cannot be accepted
An expired draw page says so clearly
A drawn result is still viewable 29 days after the draw and gone after 30
Declined, cancelled and expired draws are deleted 30 days after they ended
The sweeper runs periodically in the running app and is covered by tests with a fake clock

userStories.title: Live page updates via server-sent events
userStories.description: An open draw page updates by itself when another participant accepts, declines, or the draw happens, using a per-draw event stream authenticated by the participant key. The app still works fully without it.
acceptanceCriteria: A connected client receives a changed event after any state change
The stream requires a valid participant key and otherwise behaves like not-found
On a changed event the page refetches and re-renders
If the stream fails, the page still works through manual reload

userStories.title: Request size limits and rate limiting
userStories.description: Protect the public endpoints from abuse with a request body size limit and basic per-IP rate limiting, while leaving the number of participants uncapped.
acceptanceCriteria: Oversized request bodies are rejected with a clear status
Repeated create requests from one IP beyond the limit are rejected with 429
Normal use across a group of any size is not blocked
The limits are configurable and covered by tests

userStories.title: Deploy behind Traefik at draw-lots.lankrui.be
userStories.description: Build and run the container on the stackwise server over SSH, add the Traefik routing for draw-lots.lankrui.be without the Authentik middleware, and verify the complete flow on the live URL.
acceptanceCriteria: The container runs with a persistent volume for the SQLite file
Traefik routes draw-lots.lankrui.be to it over HTTPS with no Authentik middleware
A full flow (create, accept as all participants, drawn, reveal once) works on the live URL
Existing Traefik routes and the Authentik setup are unchanged and still work
A backup of any edited Traefik file exists before changes
